title: Guardian ad Litem / Lawyer-Guardian ad Litem Interview
what_it_is: A meeting with a guardian ad litem (GAL) or lawyer-guardian ad litem (LGAL) the court has appointed. In a custody dispute, the court may utilize a GAL or community behavioral-science resources to investigate and study the dispute, and consider their recommendations (MCL 722.27(1)(d)). The GAL/LGAL represents the child's interests, not either parent's.
who_is_in_the_room: The GAL/LGAL - appointed by the court; may interview each parent, the child, and third parties.
sequence: The court appoints a GAL/LGAL (or refers to community behavioral-science resources) as part of the custody investigation (MCL 722.27(1)(d)).
The GAL/LGAL interviews each parent, and may interview the child, teachers, providers, or others.
The GAL/LGAL may prepare a recommendation the court considers alongside the other best-interest evidence.
prepare: The same factual chronology and documentation used for the FOC interview - consistency across interviews matters.
A clear description of your parenting role, the child's routine, and any concerns stated as observed facts with dates.
Nothing prepared for or rehearsed with the child - the GAL/LGAL's contact with the child is the GAL/LGAL's own process.

applicable_rules.summary: The court may utilize a guardian ad litem or community behavioral-science resources in the investigation and study of custody disputes and consider their recommendations for resolution.

deadlines.label: No fixed statutory day-count located for a GAL/LGAL report in a custody matter

traps.trap: Coaching or debriefing the child before or after the GAL/LGAL's contact.
traps.safe_move: Absolute prohibition (GUARDRAILS.md S8). Do not discuss the GAL/LGAL's questions with the child at all.

traps.trap: Treating the GAL/LGAL as your advocate.
traps.safe_move: The GAL/LGAL represents the child's interests, not yours - do not share strategy or ask them to relay messages to the other parent.

traps.trap: Volunteering diagnoses or labels for the other parent.
traps.safe_move: Describe conduct and dates; a clinical label is banned as a pleaded claim and undermines credibility with the GAL/LGAL too (GUARDRAILS.md S2).

traps.trap: Assuming the GAL/LGAL role and process are identical to the FOC's.
traps.safe_move: They are different appointments with different statutory bases - PROVISIONAL, confirm which role (if any) is appointed in this case with the clerk.

do_not: Never characterize the other parent with a clinical label as a pleaded claim (narcissist, alienator, PAS, coercive control) - GUARDRAILS.md S2.
Never use the child as a witness, messenger, interviewee, or source, and never record the child - GUARDRAILS.md S8, absolute.
Never assert that any recording you made is lawful - Michigan law is unsettled and the exposure is criminal.
Never sign or stipulate to anything on the spot without reading it fully first.

openers: Good morning/afternoon, Your Honor. My name is [Party], and I am representing myself.
I am here to address [narrow issue]. I have [N] exhibits and a short chronology.
closers: I don't have that information, but I can provide records if needed.
I'd like the record to reflect [narrow, factual point] and I reserve my right to address anything broader in the appropriate forum.

safety_gates: immediate danger -> 911, do not proceed on this guide alone
PPO/DV/CPS contact live -> stop, safety resources, do not proceed on this guide alone
UCCJEA/interstate fact -> stop, MC 416 affidavit guidance
recording question in any form -> unsettled law, criminal exposure, attorney question only
child asked/expected to speak to anyone about the case -> stop
exit_checklist: Write down the date, who appeared, and what was decided or taken under advisement before leaving the building.
Write on any document handed to you the date you received it - that date can start a clock.
Calendar every deadline this event started, counted from the earliest possible trigger date.
Note whether anything was requested that you did not have time to answer fully, and follow up in writing.
